slides.text: Two more things to know about maps. Which types can be keys, and what a map can hold as a value. And how to overwrite entries and empty a map without losing it.

A key must be something Go can compare with `==`, because that is how the map finds it. Strings, numbers, booleans and arrays of those work. Slices, maps and functions cannot be compared, so they cannot be keys.

The snippet is pseudo code, not Go.
slides.code:
key types
    text, number, bool   -> ok
    array of those       -> ok
    list that can grow   -> not ok
    map                  -> not ok

slides.text: A value can be any type at all, including a slice. The key type is fixed when the map is made, and a key that is an array is copied when it is stored, so changing the array later does not move the entry.

slides.text:
Writing to a key that exists replaces its value, so `len` stays the same. Storing a zero is not removing: the key stays, with the value 0. Only `delete` removes a key.

The snippet is pseudo code, not Go.
slides.code:
prices has tea, milk -> 2 entries
set tea to 4   -> still 2 entries
set milk to 0  -> still 2 entries
delete milk    -> 1 entry

slides.text:
`clear` removes every entry of a map at once. The map is still the same map: it is not nil, you can write to it again, and every name that shares it sees it empty.

Setting a variable to `nil` is different: only that variable lets go of the map.
